# Why does it still look boxy? (generated by tools/why_boxy.py)

Per reference model: every class whose elements are not true geometry (decoded B-rep / saved-graphics mesh), with the count and the reason recorded during conversion. Analytical, reference, annotation and view-only categories are listed too when drawn as boxes (marked `hidden` when hidden by default).

| fidelity | meaning |
|---|---|
| matched | rebuilt from stored parameters; extents agree with Revit's bounding box, exact shape unproven |
| param | rebuilt from stored parameters; extents do NOT agree with the stored box |
| approx | a mesh exists but is incomplete / suspect (unsupported faces, wrong topology) or a rough rebuild |
| bbox | no usable geometry: drawn as a box at the stored bounding box |

## Reasons in one place

* **no saved graphics** (`symbol_no_graphics`, `no_saved_graphics`): the file stores no 3D tessellation for the element or its symbol (2D-only / annotation families, voids without cut body, reference points and hubs, rebar, MEP curves). Needs generative geometry from the reader (NEEDS-FROM-READER.md sections 3, 8).
* **MEP curves** (ducts, pipes, conduit, cable tray, flex): drawn from the stored centre curve and section (parametric, extents match); the exact fittings/transitions are not decoded.
* **mesh topology suspect**: curved faces (torus) whose triangles do not follow the surface (reader bug, NEEDS-FROM-READER.md section 10).
* **unsupported faces** (`unsupported_faces`): faces the saved-graphics tessellation skipped; the viewer adds them through OpenCascade from `element_brep` when it can (ruled / revolution / hermite / bspline), otherwise the element stays approximate.
* **structural framing/column profile families**: drawn from their saved graphics like any family instance; where Revit stores none the box remains (listed above per model).
* **family instances in 2024-2026 files**: more symbols without saved graphics and more skipped faces than 2020 (see the reader table in docs/ACCEPTANCE-STATUS.md).
